The political and macro backdrop is constructive: the Trump administration’s pro-AI, minimal-regulation stance continues to attract $2.7 trillion in domestic tech investment, while geopolitical easing (US-Iran peace deal outlines) helped push oil below $90, relieving inflation pressure. The Federal Reserve held rates at 3.5–3.75% with core CPI at 2.6%, as one dissenting vote for a cut signals rate relief is on the horizon. The critical tension to monitor is the divergence between all-time equity highs and the University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index crashing to a record low of 44.8 — historically, this gap closes either by stocks correcting or consumer confidence recovering. For FI Community, two holdings are deeply underwater (MSTR, NFLX) while two are significantly profitable (NVDA, VOO), creating a split-strategy portfolio that requires different approaches for each pair.

The ad-supported tier is scaling into a new revenue layer, live sports deals (NFL Christmas games, boxing) expand the total addressable market, and gaming and interactive content create differentiation competitors cannot easily replicate. Analysts project a 12-month target of $115 — a 32% increase from today. The socioeconomic tailwind is real: 48% of Gen Z gets financial and lifestyle content from streaming platforms, and Netflix’s position as the #1 platform is structurally protected. The US government has shown zero appetite for breaking up entertainment companies, removing regulatory risk.
holdings.rationale: Despite a slight decline this week, Netflix’s fundamentals are improving quarter over quarter. The 21% loss vs. your $110.63 cost basis is painful, but the July 16 earnings event is the catalyst most likely to recover ground. If Netflix repeats its Q1 surprise pattern (61% beat), the stock could move 10–15% in a single session. The risk of selling now and missing that recovery is greater than the risk of holding through it.

NVDA reported $81.6B in Q1 revenue (85% YoY growth) and guided Q2 to $91B, both well above estimates. Support sits at $205–210; a dip into that range is a high-conviction add opportunity. holdings.long_term_strategy: NVDA is the central nervous system of the global AI infrastructure buildout. The Trump administration’s policy of minimal AI regulation and US global leadership creates the most favorable domestic policy environment for semiconductor companies in history. The $2.7 trillion in US AI investment commitments announced in 2026 flows directly to Nvidia hardware. Blackwell architecture demand described as ‘off the charts,’ inferencing workloads expanding beyond training, and emerging robotics/edge AI applications represent a multi-year growth runway. 62 analyst Strong Buy consensus. Geopolitically, US AI policy is explicitly designed to keep Nvidia dominant. Even the $90B in AI investments to Pennsylvania alone signals the domestic policy tailwind. At 30x forward earnings, the multiple is high — but justified by 85% revenue growth and forward visibility into Q2 at $91B.

benchmarking.title: Club Benchmarking
benchmarking.subtitle: What Winning Investment Clubs Do Differently

clubs_researched.name: HBS Black Investment Club
clubs_researched.strategy: Partners directly with Apollo, Warburg Pincus, L Catterton, and Providence Equity to create a pipeline from student investors into institutional deal flow. Members research both public equities and private equity deals with a dual public/private lens.
clubs_researched.tool: Bloomberg Terminal (via university) + proprietary deal memo templates + alumni network access to institutional research
clubs_researched.takeaway: The most effective Black investment clubs build institutional relationships early — not just to learn, but to access deal flow and mentorship unavailable to retail-only investors. FI Community should identify 1–2 local financial firms or advisors willing to provide mentorship and market access.

clubs_researched.name: Spelman College Investment Club
clubs_researched.strategy: Sector rotation with quarterly rebalancing. Dedicated research leads assigned per sector. Each member owns deep expertise in 1–2 sectors and presents a 5-minute update at every meeting.
clubs_researched.tool: Google Sheets portfolio tracker + Yahoo Finance screener + Morningstar for ESG ratings
clubs_researched.takeaway: Sector ownership accountability creates members who are genuinely expert in their area. When someone ‘owns’ a sector, they read the news differently. FI Community can implement this with 4 members covering Tech, Financials, Consumer, and Macro/ETFs.

clubs_researched.name: Black Wealth Summit Network
clubs_researched.strategy: Community-first approach: financial wellness and wealth-building education as the gateway to investing. Converts financially-curious people into investors through structured curriculum before introducing stock picks.
clubs_researched.tool: Event-based community building + social media content + alumni success stories as social proof
clubs_researched.takeaway: The most successful Black wealth-building organizations lead with education and community identity, not just returns. FI Community’s brand should emphasize the journey from ‘financially curious’ to ‘fully invested’ — that narrative is a powerful recruiting and retention tool.

strategies_to_adopt.strategy: Written investment thesis requirement before any buy/sell vote
steps: Create a 1-page thesis template: ticker, 3-sentence thesis, key risks, price target (short-term 3-month and long-term 12-month), and catalysts to watch
Require submission 48 hours before any club vote on a new position
Archive all theses in a shared Google Drive folder — review them quarterly to see what was right and wrong
Assign each active member 1–2 sectors: Technology, Financials, Consumer/Retail, Macro/Policy/ETFs
Sector lead delivers a 5-minute prepared update at each meeting covering top news and any impact on club holdings
Rotate sector assignments every 6 months to build cross-functional expertise
Identify 2–3 local financial advisors, RIAs, or investment firm contacts willing to serve as mentors or guest speakers
Host a quarterly ‘Pro Insights’ meeting where an industry professional reviews your portfolio and methodology
Use these relationships to access research, tools, and eventually private deal flow as the club grows

key_insights: Elite Black investment clubs win by building institutional pipelines, not just picking stocks
Sector ownership assignments are free to implement and create genuine expertise within 90 days
Leading with financial education builds a more loyal and engaged member base than leading with returns

covered_calls.covered_call_primer: A covered call means selling someone the right to buy your shares at a set price (the strike) by a set date (expiry). You collect the premium today regardless of outcome. If the stock stays below the strike price, you keep both the shares and the full premium — pure income. If it rises above the strike, your shares get called away at the strike price — you still profit, just capped. The key: you must own at least 100 shares per contract.
